props.title: Young Törless
props.initialSlug: Student explores moral decay at elite boarding school

sections.content: **Young Törless (1966)** (1966) marks a pivotal moment in New German Cinema, with Volker Schlöndorff crafting a chilling examination of moral corruption in an Austrian military boarding school. Based on Robert Musil's novel, the film dissects how seemingly civilized youth descend into cruelty and fascism - themes that would later influence works like **If....** (1968) and The White Ribbon (2009). Schlöndorff's clinical direction and the stark black-and-white cinematography create an atmosphere of mounting dread that perfectly captures the psychological transformation of its protagonist.

sections.content: The film established Schlöndorff as a major force in New German Cinema alongside Fassbinder and Herzog. Like **Germany Year Zero** (1948), it grapples with the roots of fascism through the lens of youth. The clinical observation of cruelty anticipates later works like **Funny Games** (1997) and **The Experiment** (2001), while its boarding school setting creates a microcosm of society that would be echoed in films like **Dead Poets Society** (1989), though with far darker implications.

The film's exploration of conformity and moral corruption resonates with later works examining institutional violence. **The Wave** (2008) directly addresses how fascism can take root in schools, while **The Stanford Prison Experiment** (2015) shows how quickly power dynamics can turn ordinary people cruel. Törless's passive observation of evil parallels themes in **The Reader** (2008) and **Europa Europa** (1990). SUBHEAD: Impact on European Cinema

sections.content: Young Törless influenced a generation of European filmmakers dealing with themes of authority and moral corruption. Its DNA can be found in works like **Zero for Conduct** (1933) and **Au Revoir les Enfants** (1987), films that use the boarding school setting to examine larger societal issues. The clinical, observational style influenced Michael Haneke's entire body of work, particularly in films like **Benny's Video** (1992) and The White Ribbon (2009).
